candidateEvidence.excerpt: Jacob Coxon said in a post that he had resigned from Anthropic after three years working on AI pretraining at Anthropic and OpenAI. WIRED and ABC reported the resignation on September 9. sourceEvidence.excerpt: Published 2026-09-09T00:04:29.000Z. I resigned from Anthropic today. I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Primary September 9 resignation statement and Coxon's own allegation. Limitation: This establishes Coxon's resignation statement and stated experience. His claims about company responsibility, future systems and danger are his judgments, not independently measured findings.

WIRED reports that Coxon worked on pretraining at Anthropic and previously worked at OpenAI. Coxon told WIRED that possible threats could include AI-enabled biological threats or cyberweapons; WIRED did not establish either feared outcome as having occurred. Coxon recommends that OpenAI and Anthropic coordinate on limiting recursive self-improvement—the use of AI to build new AI systems—and ultimately seeks international coordination. Coxon said Anthropic operates more responsibly than OpenAI in his experience, but predicted that competition could force future trade-offs between rigor and safety. Asked whether Anthropic was already cutting corners, Coxon answered: No, not yet. It's not cutting any corners. Anthropic told WIRED that the industry would benefit from a lawful, verifiable way to work together to pace releases of powerful models. OpenAI did not return WIRED's request for comment.

Independent September 9 reporting based on a direct, published interview with Coxon and a response from Anthropic. Limitation: The interview is direct testimony and reporting, not an independent audit of either company, proof of future self-improving systems or validation of a catastrophe probability.
